data.gender_notes: Goat is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In ancient Greek culture, the goat was a symbol of the nourishing and providing goddesses, such as Amaltheia and Pan. In Christianity, the goat is associated with various symbols, including the Scapegoat from the Book of Leviticus and the Goat of Mendes, who was believed to bring prosperity. The name Goat carries the meaning “Nourisher, Provider” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Goat usually hope their child will grow to embody nourisher, provider and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of nourishment and provision in one's spiritual journey
data.etymology: Goat belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nourisher, Provider.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Goat total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
data.cultural_impact: In Christian tradition, the goat is often associated with the symbolism of the Scapegoat from the Jewish religious practice mentioned in the Old Testament's Book of Leviticus. During the Day of Atonement, the Israelites would place the sins of the people onto a goat and then send it into the wilderness as a symbol of confession and atonement.
data.spiritual_significance: The goat holds spiritual significance in Christianity as a symbol of repentance, atonement, and spiritual cleansing. Just as the goat bore the sins of the Israelites, Jesus Christ, the ultimate goat, bore the sins of all humanity and offered redemption and forgiveness. Additionally, the Sacrifice of Isaac in Genesis 22, which involved preparation to sacrifice a goat (later replaced by a ram), is also seen as a prefiguration of Christ's sacrifice.
